source_title: Convolutional Neural Networks - Padding and Stride
chapter_or_section: Convolutional Neural Networks - Padding and Stride
title: Calculate the output shape
instruction_text: Given the final code example in this section with kernel size (3, 5), padding (0, 1), and stride (3, 4), calculate the output shape to check if it is consistent with the experimental result.
starter_code:
def comp_conv2d(conv2d, X):
    # (1, 1) indicates that batch size and the number of channels are both 1
    X = X.reshape((1, 1) + X.shape)
    Y = conv2d(X)
    # Strip the first two dimensions: examples and channels
    return Y.reshape(Y.shape[2:])

X = torch.rand(size=(8, 8))
conv2d = nn.LazyConv2d(1, kernel_size=(3, 5), padding=(0, 1), stride=(3, 4))
comp_conv2d(conv2d, X).shape
learning_objectives: Compare how padding and stride affect convolution output size
Verify the output shape from a concrete Conv2d configuration

chapter_or_section: Keras Code Examples / Computer Vision / Simple MNIST convnet
title: Build, train, and evaluate a simple MNIST convnet
instruction_text: Build the Keras Sequential convnet for MNIST using two Conv2D layers, two MaxPooling2D layers, Flatten, Dropout, and a Dense softmax classifier. Train the model for 15 epochs with categorical_crossentropy and Adam, then evaluate the trained model on the test set.
starter_code:
model = keras.Sequential([
    keras.Input(shape=input_shape),
    layers.Conv2D(32, kernel_size=(3, 3), activation='relu'),
    layers.MaxPooling2D(pool_size=(2, 2)),
    layers.Conv2D(64, kernel_size=(3, 3), activation='relu'),
    layers.MaxPooling2D(pool_size=(2, 2)),
    layers.Flatten(),
    layers.Dropout(0.5),
    layers.Dense(num_classes, activation='softmax'),
])

model.compile(loss='categorical_crossentropy', optimizer='adam', metrics=['accuracy'])
model.fit(x_train, y_train, batch_size=128, epochs=15, validation_split=0.1)
expected_output: A trained MNIST convnet with test accuracy around 99% and reported test loss/test accuracy from model.evaluate.
constraints: Use the MNIST dataset from keras.datasets.mnist.
Use the architecture shown in the example.
